chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi 'Umayr from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What is wrong with you that you do not join 'Ali in the purchase of food? I think you are stingy.' I said: 'Yes, but if you wish, you can make it easy for me.' He said: 'Buy it.'

key_terms.وَسَّعْتَ عَلَيَّ: you make it easy for me (financially)

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say when he noticed someone was stingy with spending on food?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) addresses the narrator’s hesitation to spend on food, identifying it as a form of stinginess (dayyiq). The Imam’s instruction to proceed with the purchase serves as a practical lesson in overcoming financial constraint through voluntary spending in permissible matters, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on purifying wealth and character through generosity.
